The currently open Composite remains visible in the Library, but its insertion surface is grey and cannot be dragged into itself; its circular Update action remains available only after a real content change and then writes the open graph back to that Saved Composite. A Saved Composite's circular Update action also finds and replaces differing nested instances. Replacing with an older Saved Composite never silently deletes members that exist only in the placed instance: those nodes and complete nested Composites are moved back to their immediate parent graph, while compatible connection IDs, ports, wire points, branch routes and parent boundaries are rewritten through the previous boundary map. Boundary chains through parent and grandparent Composites are removed recursively when their source port is gone or becomes internally connected. Any affected outer wires and branch descendants are removed with that chain; a removed port is never recreated merely to preserve an old outer connection. Stable element identities make the comparison exact for new instances; legacy instances are accepted only after a deterministic structural match. If any connected element cannot be reconstructed unambiguously or the expanded result is invalid, the entire replacement is rejected and the original project remains unchanged. Every Saved Composite carries a content fingerprint derived from its normalized name, port order and side, complete node content and layout, connections, wire routes, branch routes and owned Custom C# graphs. Renaming a placed Composite to a previously unused name therefore never overwrites its former saved entry; the new name is saved as a new entry. Ambiguous duplicate normalized names are blocked instead of updating an arbitrary entry or creating another duplicate. Legacy Composite JSON without a fingerprint is offered once by exact normalized name and receives its generated fingerprint when the update is accepted. Import scope follows the matching name across both locations: a Graph-only match updates only the placed graph and creates no Saved entry; a Saved-only match updates only the library; a match in both locations updates both; only a name found nowhere is imported as new. Existing duplicate Saved entries with that exact normalized name are consolidated into one retained identity during the confirmed update. A stale or orphaned Saved-Composite identity on a placed instance never blocks the name match. If any matching Composite is open, graph replacement is blocked for the complete target set; use the Breadcrumb to open its immediate parent graph before replacing from the Node Library. Every graph replacement preserves position and every external wire route whose published endpoint still exists under the resulting contract. Updating placed graphs is intentionally available only from the matching Saved Composite's arrow action in the Node Library. An upward arrow writes the currently open Composite to the Library; a downward arrow applies the Library version to placed graph instances. If the editor state changes before the click is committed, the action refreshes and aborts instead of silently reversing direction. The action is not rendered at all while every matching placed graph has the same content fingerprint; it appears only when at least one matching graph actually differs. Removed ports are reverse-mapped before confirmation; an ambiguous mapping aborts the complete replacement instead of guessing a new endpoint. Structurally invalid outward chains and their affected wires are removed as part of the confirmed change. Every Properties action button is re-evaluated immediately after its synchronous or asynchronous action completes.
